title: Reflexivity and Alternative Theme Builder
summary: The same six invented extracts used across this module's qualitative tools, paired with one of three research questions and one of three theoretical sensitivities. Each of the nine pairings yields a prepared thematic account with its themes, a map of which extracts sit at the centre and which recede, what it illuminates and what it leaves less visible. Four pairings are strong, three workable with a stated cost, and two pull against themselves. Accounts can be saved and compared side by side, and an accountability check tests five candidate claims against the reading currently selected.
learningObjectives: Explain how a research question and a theoretical position together decide which themes are available.
Recognise a pairing in which the question and the analytic lens pull against each other.
State what a given reading illuminates and what it leaves less visible.
Distinguish several defensible readings from the claim that any reading is defensible.
Identify claims that no available reading can support, and say why in each case.
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; everything runs in the browser tab, and the tool asks nothing about the person using it.
accessibilityNotes: Native radios, selects and buttons, each with an explicit label and grouped in a fieldset with a legend. There are no charts: the foregrounding map is built from HTML and every row prints the participant's name and their standing in words - central, supporting, at the margins - so the bar length and fill are both redundant cues. The coherence rating is always printed as a word in the account card, with the coloured left border repeating it rather than carrying it. The account card and foregrounding map are pinned to the top of the stage so they stay visible while the question and lens controls beside them are changed. The comparison of two accounts is a table with row headers. Every change announces a full sentence through the polite live region including the coherence note, focus moves to the builder heading when it opens, reduced motion is honoured for the bar transition, forced-colours rules are provided, and the layout is usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths.
readmeTopic: Reflexivity: how the question and the lens decide which themes are available, and where several defensible readings stop
simulationNotes: Six invented interview extracts, shared with the Thematic Analysis Coding Laboratory and the Theme or Topic challenge in this module. Nine thematic accounts were written in advance, one per pairing of three research questions with three theoretical sensitivities; selecting a pairing selects a prepared account. The tool does not analyse anything, and does not pretend to - no software analyses qualitative data, which is part of the argument. Each pairing carries a coherence rating of strong, workable or strained, with two strained pairings included on purpose so that the mismatch between a question and a lens can be seen from outside without any appeal to the analyst's skill. The accountability check offers five claims: two fail under every reading available, one holds under every reading, one is supported by a single participant and stated as though it were about a group, and one is genuinely reading-dependent with its verdict computed from the selected lens. Nine accounts is not the space of possibilities, and the coherence ratings are judgements a supervisor could argue with. No participant, interview, institution or study is represented.
